correctness.rationale: The Hardy multiplier identity reduces the operator norm exactly to max_circle |P|^n |1-P|^k. Positivity plus p0>0 identifies every peripheral root as a gcd-root with P=1 and uniform strict contraction outside finitely many small arcs, so no off-root maximum is neglected. Cumulant expansion log|P|=-v theta^2/2+kappa4 theta^4/24+O(theta^6) and direct moment expansion of log|1-P| to theta^2 yield the first corrected Gaussian profile at x=sqrt(n)|theta|. The leading k log x-vx^2/2 has a unique, nondegenerate maximizer sqrt(k/v), and its O(1/n) displacement affects the log maximum only O(n^-2), giving k^2B. The independent Fraction calculations exactly reproduced B=-1/4, -5/16, and 145661/1401856 for the three specified distributions. The finite identities corroborate rather than replace the analytic localization and stationary-point theorem.
residual_risks: Remainder constant depends on fixed P and k, no uniformity as v->0 or k grows.
General local-limit asymptotic theorems might imply the calculation; mathematical conclusion remains directly proved.

value.rationale: A natural positive polynomial averaging operator has a sharp quantitative time-regularity profile whose first two coefficients are explicit in the law’s moments. The signed second-order correction distinguishes different convex averages even when leading scaling is the same, providing a precise usable finite-n rate classification beyond qualitative Ritt decay.
residual_risks: No general class of arbitrary Banach operators, moving k, or uniform small-variance asymptotics is asserted.

final_claim: For any fixed finite probability polynomial P with p0>0 and positive variance, T=P(S) on Hardy H2 and fixed integer k>=1, ||T^n(I-T)^k|| equals mu^k(k/(evn))^(k/2) times 1+k^2 B/n+O_(P,k)(n^-2), where B=kappa4/(24v^2)+m2^2/(8mu^2v)-m3/(6mu v); B varies in sign and equals -1/4 for every nondegenerate {0,h} law.
limitations: Fixed k, fixed nondegenerate finite-support probability law containing zero; earlier exact Bernoulli optimization credited; residual possibility of equivalent asymptotic in broader literature.
